title: An 8-bit counter, two readings
platform: Any platform for unsigned wrap-around; the signed overflow message is from the in-browser toolchain (wasm32) with its undefined-behaviour checker on.
description: An 8-bit unsigned counter is a ring of 256 patterns. Adding 1 at 255 wraps to 0, which C defines for unsigned types. The same patterns can be read as signed numbers in two's complement, where the top bit is worth minus 128: 1111 1011 is minus 128 plus 123, which is minus 5 (251 when read as unsigned). An unsigned char holding 250 plus 10 wraps to 4, but adding 1 to the largest signed int is undefined behaviour, and the browser's checker reports a signed integer overflow instead of wrapping.
